name: Toyota Motor
title: Q&A Summary of the Second-Quarter Financial Results Briefing for Investors for FY2027

read.thesis: Toyota cut treasury-share holdings from ~20% to 15% and frames FY shareholder returns at an 11–14 trillion yen range; management concedes supply bottlenecks in body-on-frame vehicles and hybrids while guiding to no FY27 operating income number.

utilisation.quote: we still need to rely partly on overtime and work on days off

capex.quote: At the current level, we expect approximately 22 trillion yen in capital expenditures and research and development expenses going forward.

triggers.label: Body-on-frame capacity lagging demand
triggers.quote: production of body-on-frame vehicles is still not keeping up with demand

triggers.label: Treasury shares cut 20% → 15%
triggers.quote: we have revised our level from 20% to 15%

triggers.label: US hybrid inventory under five days
triggers.quote: we have less than five inventory days in the United States

triggers.label: Materials cost headwind ~1.3 trillion yen
triggers.quote: we intend to fully offset higher materials prices

triggers.label: Tariff impact ~1.1 trillion yen this FY
triggers.quote: we expect the tariff impact to decline from the previous fiscal year to approximately 1.1 trillion yen

guidance.value: 11 trillion yen baseline, range 11–14 trillion yen
guidance.quote: we have set 11 trillion yen as the baseline
Dividends currently total approximately 1.2 trillion yen annually

guidance.value: approximately 1.1 trillion yen this fiscal year
guidance.quote: we expect the tariff impact to decline from the previous fiscal year to approximately 1.1 trillion yen

guidance.value: around 5 million vehicles this fiscal year
guidance.quote: We expect to reach around 5 million vehicles this fiscal year

guidance.value: 14,000 vehicles per day from second half this year into next year
guidance.quote: We are planning domestic production of 14,000 vehicles per day

guidance.value: around 150 billion yen annually as a first step
guidance.quote: maintaining growth of around 150 billion yen annually as a first step
